system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: model serving APIs
G2: Kubernetes
G3: MLflow
G4: Airflow/Kubeflow
G5: deep learning beyond a course
G6: GCP infrastructure

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
Data Scientist | Applied Machine Learning
Edinburgh, UK | tobias.mwangihartley@example.com | +44 7700 900110 |
linkedin.com/in/tmh-example
Professional Summary
Data scientist with 6 years in analytics and data science, including 4+ years as a data scientist,
focused on experimentation, forecasting and customer analytics in a subscription business. Built
operational forecasting and churn-scoring workflows using Python, BigQuery and dbt, with
measurable business outcomes. Strong statistical foundation and experience translating business
questions into analyses people act on; now moving toward machine learning engineering.
Experience
Data Scientist | Thistlebox, meal-kit subscriptions | Edinburgh Feb 2022–Present
• Design and analyse approximately 40 A/B tests per year for growth and product teams; built a
sequential testing calculator used by approximately 25 colleagues.
• Built a six-week-ahead weekly recipe and region demand forecasting workflow using LightGBM
and calendar, price and menu-position features. A scheduled notebook writes forecasts to
BigQuery for operations to use in Looker; WAPE decreased from 23% to 14%, with estimated food
waste reduction of 9%.
• Built an XGBoost churn propensity model scored weekly in BigQuery to target retention offers to

• Write production SQL in BigQuery and maintain dbt models for the analytics layer.
• Since 2025, have written pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code, reaching approximately 60%

• Built a Streamlit app for planning and analysing sequential A/B tests using statsmodels; wrote its

• Present results to leadership monthly and have delivered internal “Stats for PMs” training three
times.
Junior Data Analyst | Firth Energy Retail | Glasgow Sep 2020–Jan 2022
• Conducted customer segmentation and tariff analysis using R and SQL.
• Automated monthly regulator reports with R Markdown, saving the team approximately two days
each month.
Additional Project
Image Classification Course Project 2025
• Fine-tuned a small CNN in PyTorch on a public food-images dataset, achieving approximately
80% accuracy; a personal learning project completed as part of an online deep learning course.
Education
MSc Statistics | University of the Lothians | 2020 | Distinction
Dissertation: Bayesian hierarchical models for small-area energy demand
BSc Mathematics | University of the Lothians | 2019
Technical Skills
Python (pandas, scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, statsmodels, Streamlit); R (tidyverse, brms);
SQL (BigQuery); dbt; Git; pytest; Docker; Vertex AI Workbench scheduled notebooks; Looker; A/B
testing; causal inference; feature engineering; time-series forecasting; Bayesian statistics; PyTorch
(course project).
Languages
English (native); Swahili (conversational)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Quillstone Payments Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. My experience
combines applied machine learning, experimentation and analytics in a customer-focused
subscription business, and I am now looking to deepen my experience taking machine-learning
systems further into production.
At Thistlebox, I built a weekly demand forecasting workflow using LightGBM, with scheduled
notebook runs writing forecasts to BigQuery for operations to use in Looker. The work
reduced WAPE from 23% to 14%, with estimated food waste down 9%. I also developed a
weekly XGBoost churn-scoring workflow to target retention offers; a 10% holdout validated a
2.1 percentage-point reduction in churn in the treated group. These projects involved feature
engineering, data workflows and evaluating results against business outcomes.
I have also built a Streamlit sequential A/B testing calculator used by around 25 colleagues,
and wrote its Dockerfile; the data platform team handles its Cloud Run deployment. I bring
strong Python and SQL skills, experience with BigQuery and dbt, and have been adding
pytest unit tests to forecasting feature code, now at approximately 60% coverage. My MSc in
Statistics provides a strong foundation in modelling and uncertainty.
Quillstone’s AI team brings together engineering, data science and product to move ideas from
prototype to production and build tools that help merchants get support quickly. That
combination of applied modelling and close product and engineering collaboration is a
compelling next step for me. Thank you for considering my application; I would welcome the
opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to the team.
Kind regards, Tobias Mwangi-Hartley

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
